# Plotting tRNA structures

``` r

library(clover)
library(dplyr)
```

## Overview

clover includes pre-computed tRNA cloverleaf SVGs that can be annotated
with modification highlights, outline circles, text color changes, and
linkage arcs. This vignette walks through every customization option for
[`plot_tRNA_structure()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/plot_tRNA_structure.md)
and related functions.

## Discovering available structures

Bundled SVGs are organized by organism. Use
[`structure_organisms()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/structure_organisms.md)
to list available organisms and
[`structure_trnas()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/structure_trnas.md)
to list tRNAs within an organism.

``` r

structure_organisms()
#> [1] "Escherichia coli"         "Homo sapiens"            
#> [3] "Saccharomyces cerevisiae" "T4 phage"
```

``` r

head(structure_trnas("Escherichia coli"))
#> [1] "tRNA-Ala-GGC" "tRNA-Ala-TGC" "tRNA-Arg-ACG" "tRNA-Arg-CCG" "tRNA-Arg-CCT"
#> [6] "tRNA-Arg-TCT"
```

## Basic structure

The simplest call renders the bare cloverleaf with base-pair lines,
nucleotide letters, and position markers every 10 nucleotides.

``` r

svg <- plot_tRNA_structure("tRNA-Glu-TTC", "Escherichia coli")
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Position markers

By default, grey position numbers are drawn every 10 nucleotides. Set
`position_markers = FALSE` to hide them.

``` r

svg <- plot_tRNA_structure(
  "tRNA-Glu-TTC",
  "Escherichia coli",
  position_markers = FALSE
)
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Modification highlights

Modifications are shown as colored filled circles behind nucleotide
letters. The `modifications` argument takes a tibble with `pos` and
`mod1` columns. Output from
[`modomics_mods()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/modomics_mods.md)
works directly after filtering to the tRNA of interest.

``` r

fasta_path <- clover_example("ecoli/trna_only.fa.gz")
mods <- modomics_mods(fasta_path, "Escherichia coli")
#> Processing 182 MODOMICS sequences.
#> Matching MODOMICS sequences to reference FASTA.
#> Found 701 modification annotations.

mods_glu <- mods |>
  filter(ref == "host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1")
mods_glu
#> # A tibble: 11 × 4
#>    ref                     pos mod_full                          mod1   
#>    <chr>                 <int> <chr>                             <chr>  
#>  1 host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1    13 pseudouridine                     Y      
#>  2 host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1    35 5-methylaminomethyl-2-thiouridine mnm5s2U
#>  3 host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1    38 2-methyladenosine                 m2A    
#>  4 host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1    54 5-methyluridine                   m5U    
#>  5 host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1    55 pseudouridine                     Y      
#>  6 host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1     8 4-thiouridine                     s4U    
#>  7 host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1    13 pseudouridine                     Y      
#>  8 host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1    35 5-methylaminomethyl-2-thiouridine mnm5s2U
#>  9 host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1    38 2-methyladenosine                 m2A    
#> 10 host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1    54 5-methyluridine                   m5U    
#> 11 host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1    55 pseudouridine                     Y
```

Since
[`plot_tRNA_structure()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/plot_tRNA_structure.md)
uses 1-based sequence positions, we load Sprinzl coordinates to convert
named positions (like the anticodon at Sprinzl 34-36) to their actual
sequence indices.

``` r

sprinzl <- read_sprinzl_coords(
  clover_example("sprinzl/ecoliK12_global_coords.tsv.gz")
)
glu_coords <- sprinzl |>
  filter(trna_id == "tRNA-Glu-UUC-1-1")
```

``` r

svg <- plot_tRNA_structure(
  "tRNA-Glu-TTC",
  "Escherichia coli",
  modifications = mods_glu
)
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Custom modification palettes

[`default_mod_palette()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/default_mod_palette.md)
returns a named character vector mapping modification short names to
colors. You can extend or override it.

``` r

head(default_mod_palette(), 10)
#>       m1A       m1G       m2A       m2G     m2,2G       m3C       m5C       m5U 
#> "#E41A1C" "#984EA3" "#E68A00" "#66C2A5" "#8DA0CB" "#B3DE69" "#377EB8" "#FF7F00" 
#>       m6A     m6t6A 
#> "#FB9A99" "#D95F02"
```

To add a custom category (e.g., highlighting anticodon positions),
combine MODOMICS modifications with your own entries and extend the
palette.

``` r

# Add anticodon positions (Sprinzl 34-36) as a custom category
ac_pos <- glu_coords |>
  filter(sprinzl_label %in% c("34", "35", "36")) |>
  pull(pos)

anticodon <- tibble::tibble(
  pos = ac_pos,
  mod1 = rep("anticodon", 3)
)

all_mods <- bind_rows(mods_glu, anticodon)

# Extend the palette with a color for the new category
custom_palette <- c(default_mod_palette(), anticodon = "#4DAF4A")

svg <- plot_tRNA_structure(
  "tRNA-Glu-TTC",
  "Escherichia coli",
  modifications = all_mods,
  mod_palette = custom_palette
)
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Outline circles

Outlines draw stroke-only circles around nucleotides, useful for
highlighting positions without covering the base letter. The `outlines`
argument takes a tibble with `pos` and `group` columns;
`outline_palette` maps group names to colors.

``` r

# Highlight the discriminator base (Sprinzl position 73)
disc_pos <- glu_coords |>
  filter(sprinzl_label == "73") |>
  pull(pos)

disc_outline <- tibble::tibble(pos = disc_pos, group = "discriminator")

svg <- plot_tRNA_structure(
  "tRNA-Glu-TTC",
  "Escherichia coli",
  outlines = disc_outline,
  outline_palette = c(discriminator = "#E41A1C")
)
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Text colors

Use `text_colors` to change the color of nucleotide letters at specific
positions. This takes a tibble with `pos` and `color` columns.

``` r

# Color the anticodon triplet (Sprinzl 34-36) green
ac_text <- tibble::tibble(
  pos = ac_pos,
  color = rep("#4DAF4A", 3)
)

svg <- plot_tRNA_structure(
  "tRNA-Glu-TTC",
  "Escherichia coli",
  text_colors = ac_text
)
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Combining annotations

Modifications, outlines, and text colors can all be used together.

``` r

disc_outline <- tibble::tibble(pos = disc_pos, group = "discriminator")
disc_text <- tibble::tibble(pos = disc_pos, color = "#E41A1C")

svg <- plot_tRNA_structure(
  "tRNA-Glu-TTC",
  "Escherichia coli",
  modifications = all_mods,
  mod_palette = custom_palette,
  outlines = disc_outline,
  outline_palette = c(discriminator = "#E41A1C"),
  text_colors = disc_text
)
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Linkage arcs

Pairwise modification co-occurrence can be visualized as arcs on the
cloverleaf. The `linkages` argument takes a tibble with `pos1`, `pos2`,
and optionally `value` columns. If a `log_odds_ratio` column is present
(as in output from
[`clean_odds_ratios()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/clean_odds_ratios.md)
/
[`filter_linkages()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/filter_linkages.md)),
it is used automatically.

Arc color encodes direction: blue for mutual exclusivity (negative log
OR) and vermillion for co-occurrence (positive log OR). Stroke width
encodes magnitude.

``` r

or_path <- clover_example(
  "ecoli/summary/tables/wt-15-ctl-01/wt-15-ctl-01.odds_ratios_filtered.tsv.gz"
)
or_data <- read_odds_ratios(or_path)

linkages_glu <- or_data |>
  filter(ref == "host-tRNA-Glu-TTC-1-1") |>
  clean_odds_ratios() |>
  filter_linkages()
```

``` r

svg <- plot_tRNA_structure(
  "tRNA-Glu-TTC",
  "Escherichia coli",
  modifications = mods_glu,
  linkages = linkages_glu
)
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Custom linkage palettes

The `linkage_palette` parameter is a character vector of length 2: the
first color is used for negative values (exclusive), the second for
positive values (co-occurring). The default is
`c("#0072B2", "#D55E00")`.

``` r

svg <- plot_tRNA_structure(
  "tRNA-Glu-TTC",
  "Escherichia coli",
  linkages = linkages_glu,
  linkage_palette = c("#7570B3", "#D95F02")
)
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Long variable arm tRNAs

Leu and Ser tRNAs have a long variable arm with an extra stem-loop.
These are properly rendered from the tRNAscan-SE covariance model
alignment.

``` r

svg <- plot_tRNA_structure("tRNA-Leu-CAA", "Escherichia coli")
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

``` r

svg <- plot_tRNA_structure("tRNA-Ser-GGA", "Escherichia coli")
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Identity elements

[`plot_identity_structure()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/plot_identity_structure.md)
overlays experimentally validated aminoacylation identity elements (from
Giege & Eriani, 2023) onto the cloverleaf. Strong determinants are
outlined in red, weak determinants in blue.

This requires Sprinzl coordinates to map element positions onto the tRNA
sequence. Bundled coordinate files are available for *E. coli* and *S.
cerevisiae*.

``` r

coords <- read_sprinzl_coords(
  clover_example("sprinzl/sacCer_global_coords.tsv.gz")
)

svg <- plot_identity_structure(
  "tRNA-Ala-AGC",
  "Saccharomyces cerevisiae",
  coords
)
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

### Identity element panel

[`plot_identity_panel()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/plot_identity_panel.md)
arranges multiple tRNAs in a grid, each annotated with its amino acid
family’s identity elements. Use `ncol` to control the number of columns.

``` r

svg <- plot_identity_panel(
  c("tRNA-Ala-AGC", "tRNA-Asp-GTC", "tRNA-Phe-GAA", "tRNA-His-GTG"),
  "Saccharomyces cerevisiae",
  coords,
  ncol = 2
)
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Output formats

[`plot_tRNA_structure()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/plot_tRNA_structure.md)
writes an SVG file and returns the path invisibly. For embedding in R
Markdown or Quarto, use
[`structure_html()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/structure_html.md)
to wrap the SVG in a centered `<div>`. For raster output, use
[`structure_to_png()`](https://rnabioco.github.io/clover/reference/structure_to_png.md).

``` r

# Embed as HTML (used throughout this vignette)
svg <- plot_tRNA_structure("tRNA-Glu-TTC", "Escherichia coli")
structure_html(svg)

# Convert to PNG
png <- structure_to_png(svg, width = 600)
```
